title: How to Apply for Caste Certificate Online - SC/ST/OBC 2026
meta_description: Caste certificate application 2026 - how to apply SC/ST/OBC online state-wise. Documents needed, state portals, processing time 15-30 days.

hero.one_liner: Caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC) is essential for availing 15-27% reservation in government jobs and education. Apply online through your state e-District portal in 3 steps.

sections.heading: Why a Caste Certificate Matters
content: A caste certificate is your official proof of belonging to a Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, or Other Backward Class. It is your legal key to constitutional reservation in jobs and education.
Without a valid one, you cannot claim reservation seats in UPSC, SSC, banking, railways, or state PSC exams, nor reserved seats and fee concessions in colleges.
The certificate itself is free in most states, or costs a small fee, and is issued by the district revenue authority.
About 70% of India's population belongs to a reserved category, which is why this single document shapes access to so many jobs and college seats.
It is issued once by the district revenue authority and then asked for again and again across your education and career, so getting it right early pays off for years.

sections.heading: SC vs ST vs OBC: What Each Means
content: Scheduled Castes are communities historically subjected to untouchability, listed under Article 341. They get 15% central reservation, and the SC certificate is permanent with no income ceiling.
Scheduled Tribes are tribal communities listed under Article 342, based on geographic and ethnic criteria. They get 7.5% reservation, also permanent with no income limit.
Other Backward Classes are socially and educationally backward groups identified by the NCBC. They get 27% central reservation, but with a creamy layer income exclusion.
ST communities also benefit from the PESA Act for self-governance in scheduled areas and the Forest Rights Act. These add to the reservation in jobs and education.
For OBC, the central list and state list can differ, so always confirm which list applies to the specific exam or admission you are targeting.
SC reservation is 15% and ST 7.5% in central jobs and education, while OBC is 27%, though state percentages vary widely.
Knowing your exact category and the right list saves you from claiming a benefit your certificate does not actually unlock.

sections.heading: Online and Offline Application Routes
content: Most states accept online applications on the e-District portal, where you register, pick Caste Certificate, fill the form, upload documents, and pay a small fee.
Offline, you visit the Tehsildar or SDM office, fill the form, and submit documents for field verification. Online usually takes 7 to 15 days, offline 15 to 30 days.
For central use like UPSC or SSC, the certificate must be in the prescribed central format, which can differ from the plain state format.
Whichever route you use, the issuing officer must be an authorised authority such as the District Magistrate, Additional DM, or SDM. A certificate from the wrong officer can be rejected.
Keep your acknowledgement or application number safe, since you will need it to track the status and to follow up if verification stalls.

sections.heading: Document Details and Substitutes
content: The strongest evidence is your father's caste certificate, backed by a family ration card showing the caste entry and your school leaving certificate.
If your father's certificate is missing, use your grandfather's certificate or a community certificate from the village Sarpanch attesting your caste.
Aadhaar is mandatory in most states for online filing, along with a residence proof. For OBC-NCL, add parental income proof such as the latest ITR.
If a parent is a government employee in a senior specified position, the family may fall into the OBC creamy layer, and the plain OBC certificate alone will not give central reservation.
Keep a self-declaration affidavit on stamp paper ready, since many states ask for it alongside community member affidavits confirming your caste.
A community or mohalla certificate from the village Sarpanch or Pradhan is a recognised substitute when family certificates are missing, especially in rural areas.
For migrants, a domicile or residence proof showing your years in the state is often required before the caste certificate is issued.
Always carry the originals when offline verification is needed, since the officer compares them against your uploaded scans.
Where a document is genuinely unavailable, the affidavit and community confirmation route exists precisely so that no eligible person is shut out.

sections.heading: How Much It Costs and How Long It Takes
content: The caste certificate is free or nearly free in most states, with fees usually between Rs 10 and Rs 50. Beware of agents who charge hundreds for what you can do yourself.
Online applications are typically issued in 7 to 15 days, while office applications take 15 to 30 days. Maharashtra's separate Caste Validity step can take 3 to 6 months.
Plan around these timelines, since a missing certificate at an exam deadline can cost you the reserved seat entirely.
Online portals usually let you track each stage, from Patwari verification to SDM approval, so you know exactly where your file is.
If a file sits at pending verification beyond about fifteen days, a polite in-person follow-up at the office often moves it along.

sections.title: OBC Creamy Layer: The Rs 8 Lakh Rule
sections.content:
For central OBC reservation you need both an OBC caste certificate and a Non-Creamy Layer certificate. Creamy layer means family income above Rs 8 lakh a year from non-agricultural, non-salary sources.

Agricultural income is excluded, and recent rules say salary alone may not push you into creamy layer. A parent in a Group A post makes the family creamy layer regardless of income.

sections.title: OBC-NCL Certificate Validity
sections.desc:
SC and ST certificates are permanent, issued once and valid for life. The OBC caste certificate is also permanent.

But the OBC Non-Creamy Layer certificate is valid for only one year for central use, and must be renewed. For a central exam, it must be issued in the current financial year.

sections.heading: If Your Application Gets Rejected
content: The top reason is caste not recognised, meaning your caste is not on the relevant list. Check the official NCBC, NCSC, or NCST list, since some castes are on state lists but not central ones.
A failed Patwari verification means the officer could not confirm your caste from records. Provide stronger community affidavits and your father's certificate.
A name mismatch with school records is common. Fix your Aadhaar name or get the Patwari to note that both names refer to the same person.
A domicile mismatch is another common reason, where your records show one state but you apply in another. A domicile certificate or residence proof fixes this.
Some states require several years of residency proof before issuing a caste certificate to people who migrated from another state, so check the local rule.
If your caste is missing from both central and state lists, you cannot claim that reservation, and pushing a wrong claim only wastes months.
When a certificate is rejected, fix the specific stated reason and reapply, rather than submitting the same papers again.

sections.heading: What Happens at Document Verification
content: At a government job check, the officer confirms the certificate is from a competent authority, in the prescribed format, and that an OBC-NCL is valid for the year. Any discrepancy can cancel your candidature, even after appointment.

At college admission, the office checks your caste against the central or state list. Maharashtra additionally needs a separate Caste Validity Certificate from the Scrutiny Committee, which takes 3 to 6 months.
Submitting a fake certificate is a criminal offence, and detection has become far more digital and cross-referenced. Start any validity process early, well before verification.
The Maharashtra Caste Validity Certificate comes from the Caste Scrutiny Committee and is mandatory there for government jobs and admissions. Begin it early, not at the last minute.
Because verification is now cross-referenced digitally, a genuine certificate in the correct format clears quickly, while any gap stands out fast.
Keep the certificate's format matched to the authority you are applying to, since a state-format certificate may not be accepted for a central post.
If you are selected provisionally, complete any pending validity step quickly, because a gap found later can undo the appointment.

sections.heading: Special Cases: Adoption, Mixed Parentage
content: Caste is generally patrilineal, so you inherit your father's caste and apply using his certificate. If you believe your caste differs, you may need a formal community and revenue process.
If your parents are from different states, apply in the state where you are currently domiciled, where your Aadhaar and voter ID are.
If you are adopted, you use your adoptive father's caste with the adoption documents and his certificate. Your biological caste does not matter legally once adopted into the community.
Some institutions may accept a certificate from either parent's state of origin, but the standard rule is to use your current state of residence.
When records conflict, a clear paper trail, the father's certificate, school records, and community confirmation, is what carries an application through.
Adoption documents plus the adoptive father's caste certificate are usually enough, and the community's acceptance carries weight in verification.
For inter-state parentage, your domicile decides the state, so keep your Aadhaar and voter records consistent with where you actually live.

sections.heading: State Portals and Processing Times
content: Delhi uses edistrict.delhigovt.nic.in with about 7 to 10 days processing, UP uses edistrict.up.gov.in, and Bihar uses serviceonline.bihar.gov.in.
Maharashtra uses aaplesarkar.mahaonline.gov.in, with a separate Caste Validity step for some categories. Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Telangana each have their own seva portals.
For states without a full online system, like West Bengal, you apply through the BDO or SDO office. Track your status and follow up in person if it is stuck beyond 15 days.
Fees are small, usually between Rs 10 and Rs 50, and most portals let you pay by net banking or card. Save the acknowledgement number to track your application.
Apply two to three months before any deadline, since online filings are usually faster than office visits but still need verification time.
West Bengal and a few states still run largely offline through the BDO or SDO office, so factor in extra time there.
Wherever you apply, a clear set of documents and a matching name across them is what makes the difference between a fast approval and a stalled file.

sections.title: Apply 2 to 3 Months Before You Need It
sections.content:
Processing takes 7 to 30 days depending on the state and method. If your exam deadline is in June, apply for the certificate in April.

This buffer covers verification delays and any document correction, so you are never caught short at the application deadline.

sections.title: Central and State OBC Lists Are Different
sections.content:
Your caste may be OBC in your state's list but not on the central list, or the other way round. For central exams like UPSC, SSC, IBPS, and Railways, only the central list counts.

Always check the NCBC list at ncbc.nic.in before claiming central reservation, so your certificate is actually accepted.

sections.text: The caste certificate is the most important document for 70% of India's population that belongs to SC, ST, or OBC categories. It unlocks 50% of government job seats, 50% of educational institution seats, and access to hundreds of welfare schemes with enhanced benefits. Without it, constitutional reservation rights exist only on paper. Apply at your state's e-District portal - the process takes 10 minutes online. The impact lasts a lifetime.

sections.heading: Keeping Your Certificate Usable Over Time
content: An SC or ST certificate is permanent, so once issued you keep it for life and simply produce it when needed.
An OBC-NCL must be kept current, so renew it before each financial year if you are applying for central jobs. Track when it expires.
Always keep both a printed copy and a scanned PDF, since exam and admission portals usually need an upload and offices often want a hard copy.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes That Delay Approval
content: The most common delay is a name or spelling mismatch between your Aadhaar, school records, and the application. Make them match before you submit.
Another is applying with a caste that is on the state list but not the central list, then using it for a central exam. Confirm the right list first.
Uploading blurry or incomplete documents also stalls verification, so scan clearly and include every required paper the first time.

sections.title: Official Sources and References
sections.content:
This page is based on the rules of the District Magistrate office and the SC, ST, and OBC reservation guidelines, verified against official notifications.

For the current lists and formats, always check NCBC, NCSC, NCST, and your own state e-District portal before applying.

faqs.question: Is caste certificate valid for lifetime or does it expire?
faqs.answer:
SC/ST caste certificates are valid for lifetime in most states. OBC certificates are also lifetime, but OBC-NCL (Non-Creamy Layer) certificates are valid for only 1 year and must be renewed annually.

Check your specific state's rules and the certificate itself - it should mention validity period. For central government jobs, you don't need recent certificate as long as it was issued by a competent authority (SDM/Tehsildar).

faqs.question: My school doesn't mention caste on my leaving certificate. How do I prove caste?
faqs.answer:
School records are the easiest proof, but not the only way. If your school certificate doesn't mention caste (which is common for students from urban/private schools), use: (1) Father's caste certificate, (2) Ration card showing your category, (3) Land records from Patwari showing family caste, (4) Affidavits from 4-5 community members.

The Patwari will verify from revenue office records that date back 20-30 years.

faqs.question: I belong to a caste that's OBC in my state but General in another state. Which category applies?
faqs.answer:
You follow your state of domicile's caste list. If you're domiciled in State A where your caste is OBC, you get OBC status.

If you move to State B where the same caste is not OBC, you don't get OBC benefits in State B. For central jobs, you must follow the central OBC list.

Always check which list applies to your situation before applying.

faqs.question: Can I get caste certificate if my father is from one state and I'm born in another?
faqs.answer:
Yes. You can get caste certificate in either: (1) Your father's state of origin (using his caste certificate), or (2) Your current domicile state (using Aadhaar and residency proof).

If you apply in a different state from your father's, you may need additional documents like domicile proof. Applying in your current state of residence is usually easier.

faqs.question: What's the difference between 'Caste Certificate' and 'Community Certificate'?
faqs.answer:
'Caste Certificate' is the formal government-issued document confirming your SC/ST/OBC status. 'Community Certificate' is sometimes issued by gram panchayat or community leaders (informal).

For official purposes (government jobs, education), you need the formal caste certificate from SDM/Tehsildar, not community certificate. However, community certificate can be useful initial proof while applying for formal caste certificate.

faqs.question: I'm applying for UPSC and need OBC-NCL certificate. My state hasn't renewed it since last year. What do I do?
faqs.answer:
For UPSC (and most central recruitments), the OBC-NCL certificate must be valid on the notification date or closing date of application. If your certificate expired, immediately apply for renewal in your state portal.

Processing takes 7-15 days. Apply urgently - if not received by closing date, you cannot claim OBC benefit for that exam.

Plan ahead and renew before expiry.

faqs.question: The Patwari says my caste is not in records. I've lived here 20 years. What now?
faqs.answer:
If revenue records don't show your caste but you've lived in the community for 20 years, get strong community evidence: (1) Get 5-6 neighbors/community members (preferably from your caste community) to sign affidavits on ₹10 stamp paper, (2) Get gram panchayat's statement confirming you're part of the community, (3) Show long residence: ration card, property records, children's school records from the area. Resubmit with these documents.

The Tehsildar has discretion to issue based on community acceptance.

faqs.question: Can I apply for caste certificate while my father's certificate is being processed?
faqs.answer:
It's possible but slower. If you apply without father's certificate, the Patwari will take longer to verify your caste (20-30 days instead of 7-15 days).

Wait for father's certificate to be issued first if possible - it significantly speeds up your approval. If urgent, apply without waiting but understand the delay.

faqs.question: How to get caste certificate online?
faqs.answer:
Visit your state's e-District portal (edistrict.up.gov.in for UP, serviceonline.bihar.gov.in for Bihar, etc.) → Register → Select 'Caste Certificate/Jati Praman Patra' → Fill form with personal and caste details → Upload documents (father's certificate, ration card, Aadhaar) → Pay fee (Rs 10-50) → Submit. Processing: 7-30 days.

Download the certificate from the portal after approval.

faqs.question: Is caste certificate valid for lifetime?
faqs.answer:
SC/ST certificates: Generally permanent (some states issue with 3-5 year validity but renewal is a formality). OBC certificates: The caste certificate itself may be permanent, but the NON-CREAMY LAYER certificate must be renewed periodically (annually or every 3 years depending on state).

Without valid non-creamy layer certificate, OBC reservation benefits cannot be claimed.

faqs.question: Can I get caste certificate from a different state?
faqs.answer:
Your caste certificate must be issued by the state where your family is ORIGINALLY domiciled - not where you currently live. If your family is originally from Bihar but you live in Delhi, you need a Bihar caste certificate (issued by Bihar authorities).

Some states allow the local SDM to issue certificates for domiciles of other states - but for central government purposes, the HOME STATE certificate is strongest.

faqs.question: What if my caste is in state OBC list but not central?
faqs.answer:
For state government jobs and state university admissions: your state OBC certificate works. For central government exams (UPSC, SSC, IBPS, Railways): you CANNOT claim OBC reservation because your caste isn't in the central list.

Apply as general/EWS category for central exams. Check central OBC list at ncbc.nic.in and state list at your state backward classes commission website.

faqs.question: Is a caste certificate valid for life?
faqs.answer:
SC and ST caste certificates are permanent and valid for life. The OBC caste certificate is also permanent.

But the OBC Non-Creamy Layer certificate is valid for only one year for central use and must be renewed.

faqs.question: What is the income limit for OBC non-creamy layer?
faqs.answer:
The OBC non-creamy layer income limit is Rs 8 lakh a year, counted from non-agricultural and non-salary sources. Agricultural income is excluded.

If your family income crosses this, or a parent holds a Group A post, you fall into the creamy layer and lose central OBC reservation.

disclaimer: Caste certificate procedures and OBC/SC/ST lists vary by state and central government. This guide is based on common practices as of March 2026. Always verify specific requirements with your state's revenue department.
